Like a motherfuckin' boss.

Vaughn was a true master of his instrument. Some credit for that change goes to his guitar tech/stage hand. A good tech will have the other strung and back in tune in about three minutes - they will have strings already out and set where they can grab them in low light.

But, let this video stand as an example! Do not go on stage without spares. Not even SRV is good enough to go out without spares. Always have spares. That means carrying a heavy load and doubles of some pretty hefty gear. Even your amps should have spares that sit in the truck. If you're at the point where you have stacks, you should have at least one full spare stack - if not two.

Strings? Bring a half dozen sets. Cords? Bring triple what you need. Pedals? Have a spare of each and every pedal. (Those go through a lot of abuse, I'm partial to Boss brand 'cause they hold up like a Boss.) Big show and you're not going to be able to grab rented gear in an emergency? Bring a small electronics repair kit.

Shit breaks when you're lugging stuff in and out of the venue once a week (or even more often). I've knocked a guitar off the stand and promptly tripped, stepped on it, broke the neck, and then fallen flat on my back. (I can even remember the exact moment that all went down, too!)

You got a Fender Strat? Order a spare neck now. (You don't need to carry that with you, 'cause you'll be carrying a second Strat with you - or at least another electric from which you can get the appropriate tone.)

I can't stress this enough - always have spare gear. Always. Even if you don't perform, have spare gear. It'd really suck to have your guitar break and be unable to play for the month or two it takes you to find and buy a new one. Always, always have spare gear. Tubes? Have dozens of them in various sizes. Cords? You can't have enough. Strings? Buy in bulk - you'll save money that way. Picks? Those can be ordered by the box - you can even get boxes of 1000 - don't go on stage with fewer than 20 in your pockets and have 20 more for each set. You will drop them and sometimes you get into the spirit of things and throw 'em to someone in the audience. They break, they chip, they get dirty and sweaty. Have spares. (Not applicable if you're fingerpicking - you can't really bring spare fingers.)
